body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 3b92beeb9e4932fd4758bca6849e55870fd72810 -->
**Needs changes before merge** - one small fix: the new "Open <name> fixtures" button skips the setup activation that every other way into a setup's Fixtures page does, so on an inactive setup it lands on a page without the workholding.

### What looks good
- The no-setup Setups page loses the workholding block and the tool list, and nothing a user could do there is lost: both stay reachable from the browser's implicit Fixtures and Tool list rows, which already stand under Setup with no setups (pinned by `setup_tree::every_setup_owns_its_nodes_in_order`). The decision note records the choice for the tool list, as the issue asked.
- The setup-node page is drawn inside a vertical `ScrollArea` (`pages.rs:123`), so the button is still reachable at the default pane size by scrolling.
- The pointer lines are plain English and correct: the browser's top node is "Setup", and the implicit nodes sit under it.
- `setup_page_alignment_rows_structure` is untouched and still passes. The #1104 test keeps every assertion, and the renamed no-setup test now asserts the opposite of the old behaviour, which is what the issue asks for.
- Layering is fine: no Flecs in ui, and the button changes view state only through `actions::target`. No snapshot PNG, process file, `Cargo` file or `CHANGELOG.md` changed. `pages.rs` is down by 2 lines (1757 -> 1755). The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #1197`, and the commit subjects are conventional.

### Local results (trial-merged with main 3aa8f3ef, merge was clean)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (the plan: ui lib, boundary, boundary_picks, theme_files) | ok, 203 s |
| camcraft-ui lib unit tests | 594 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored |
| ui:boundary / boundary_picks / theme_files | 3 / 6 / 14 passed |
| Named: `setups_declutter` (3), `structural::setup_page_alignment_rows_structure`, `setup_tree` (7) | 11 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
1. **`crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_pages.rs:180-182`: activate the setup before opening its Fixtures page.** The browser's Fixtures row (`browser_pane.rs:160-162`) and the Setups page's "Open page" button (`pages.rs:755-758`, commented "the fixture and tool pages edit only the active setup") both call `browser_pane::focus(state, name)` before `actions::target`. The new button calls only `actions::target`. A user reaches an inactive setup's Settings page with a plain left-click on its browser node (`browser_pane.rs:143` does not activate). From there, "Open Setup2 fixtures" opens a Fixtures page that `editable()` (`setup_pages.rs:80-91`) blocks with "Setup2 is not the active setup - activate it ...". That page shows no workholding, so in the several-setups state the "one obvious click" does not reach it. The fix is one line: `super::browser_pane::focus(state, name);` before the `target` call. Please also add a pin, e.g. in `one_setup_...` or the two-setup fixture: with Setup1 active, open Setup2's Settings page, click "Open Setup2 fixtures", and assert that Setup2 is active and its Fixtures page shows "orkholding".

### Notes (not blocking)
- **Placement.** "Open <name> fixtures" sits next to "Delete <name>" on the last line of a long page, below the fold at the default pane size (the test needs a 1280x1400 pane to click it). The button works, and the browser's Fixtures row stays one visible click away in every state. So this does not block the issue, but the button is a weak signpost. A short pointer line plus button near the top of the page would be easier to find, and moving it would also take it away from the destructive button. A gap (`ui.add_space`) or putting Delete last on the line would help as well. Mis-clicking Delete is recoverable, since DeleteSetup is an undoable command.
- **The two pointer texts differ.** The Setups page says "Its fixtures and tools are in the browser, under Setup.", and the implicit Settings page says "Its fixtures are under Fixtures in the browser, not on this page." One shared wording, ideally naming both Fixtures and Tool list, would read better.
- The Setup<n> Settings page still has the "Workholding max rpm" row (#1031). That is a setup setting, not the workholding block, and the decision note says so. Fine as is.
- The decision note says "P3, effort:medium" (the issue is now effort:high) and "pinned by the existing fixture UX test" for the implicit Fixtures row. That pin is actually `setup_tree::every_setup_owns_its_nodes_in_order`; `fixture_ux_tests` checks Setup1 only.
- The two-setup state reaches Fixtures only through `actions::target` in the test. Neither the browser rows nor the new button is clicked there. The requested pin above covers the button.

### Not exercised
Nothing was looked at on screen (no GUI launch). Snapshot lanes not run (release-lane).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: f9a0818e47bece30a42b3802868c4008d162cd21 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** The blocker from the review of `3b92beeb` is fixed, and the new test pins the fix.

### What looks good
- **Only one commit since `3b92beeb` (`f9a0818e`), and it changes only what it says it does.** `git diff 3b92beeb f9a0818e --stat` shows 4 files, +50/-5: the one `focus` call, the shared pointer constant, the new test and the decision note.
- **The setup is now activated the same way a browser click does it.** "Open <name> fixtures" calls `super::browser_pane::focus(state, name)` before `actions::target` (`setup_pages.rs:185-188`). That is the same path the browser's Fixtures row (`browser_pane.rs:160-162`) and "Open page" use. `focus` queues `CommandKind::ActivateSetup`, an undoable command, so the field is not poked directly.
- **The new test proves the fix.** `an_inactive_setups_fixtures_button_activates_it_and_opens_its_workholding` asserts that Setup2 becomes active, that its Fixtures page opens without the "not the active setup" refusal, and that it shows the workholding. I removed the `focus` call locally (never pushed) and the test fails as it should:
  ```
  assertion `left == right` failed: the button activates Setup2, as a browser click on its Fixtures row does
    left: Some("Setup1")
   right: Some("Setup2")
  ```
  With the call restored, it passes.
- **The two pointer lines now share one wording.** Both use `WORKHOLDING_POINTER`, which reads "Fixtures and tools are under Setup in the browser, not on this page." That is plain English, and it names the browser's actual "Setup" node. The decision note is corrected.

### Local results (trial-merged with main 7a5816cf, merge was clean)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-ui lib unit tests | 607 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored |
| Named: `setups_declutter` (4), `structural::setup_page_alignment_rows_structure` (1), `setup_tree` (7) | 12 passed |
| New test with the `focus` call removed (local only) | fails as expected (above) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
- **A doc comment moved to the wrong constant.** `WORKHOLDING_POINTER` was inserted between `ACTIVE_SETUP_LABEL`'s doc comment and the constant itself (`setup_pages.rs:137-143`). Both doc blocks now attach to `WORKHOLDING_POINTER`, and `ACTIVE_SETUP_LABEL` has none. Moving the new constant above that doc comment fixes it. This can go in any later touch.
- **The button's placement is unchanged.** It is still on the Delete line, below the fold at the default pane size but reachable by scrolling. The browser's Fixtures row stays one visible click away in every state. This was already noted in the first review.

### Not exercised
Nothing was looked at on screen. The snapshot lanes were not run (they run only at a release cut).

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
